title: Jupiter and the Tortoise
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: Jupiter was about to marry a wife, and determined to celebrate the event by inviting all the animals to a banquet. They all came except the Tortoise, who did not put in an appearance, much to Jupiter's surprise. So when he next saw the Tortoise he asked him why he had not been at the banquet. "I don't care for going out," said the Tortoise; "there's no place like home." Jupiter was so much annoyed by this reply that he decreed that from that time forth the Tortoise should carry his house upon his back, and never be able to get away from home even if he wished to.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what event does Jupiter celebrate with a banquet?
options: The birth of a new god
The end of a long war
His marriage to a wife
The founding of a new city

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who is invited to the banquet?
options: All the animals
Only the gods of Olympus
Only the birds and fish
Only the animals who had helped Jupiter before

questions.prompt: According to the passage, which animal fails to attend the banquet?
options: The Fox
The Eagle
The Lion
The Tortoise

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Jupiter ask the Tortoise when he next sees him?
options: Where he had been hiding all this time
Why he had not been at the banquet
Whether he was feeling unwell
Why he never speaks at gatherings

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what reason does the Tortoise give for not attending?
options: "I was too slow to arrive in time."
"I was never told about the banquet."
"There's no place like home."
"I do not eat the food served at banquets."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does Jupiter react to the Tortoise's reply?
options: He is so annoyed that he decrees a permanent punishment
He laughs and forgives the Tortoise at once
He invites the Tortoise to a second banquet
He asks the other animals to explain the Tortoise's absence

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Jupiter decree the Tortoise must do from then on?
options: Live apart from all the other animals
Attend every future banquet without exception
Give up his home entirely
Carry his house upon his back

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does Jupiter's punishment fit the Tortoise's own words so precisely?
options: It forces the Tortoise to attend every banquet Jupiter holds from then on
It ensures the Tortoise is never without his home, even though he can no longer be truly free of the world outside it
It removes the Tortoise's home entirely as a punishment
It gives the Tortoise a new home better than his old one

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "decreed" mean in "he decreed that from that time forth"?
options: Quietly suggested
Politely requested
Officially ordered or declared
Secretly planned

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: A preference taken to an extreme can be turned into a permanent condition
Jupiter is always fair in how he punishes those who offend him
Tortoises are naturally suited to carrying heavy loads
Banquets are the best way to test loyalty among animals

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does Jupiter feel about the Tortoise's absence at first?
options: Angry
Indifferent
Amused
Surprised

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Tortoise say he does not care for?
options: Eating at large gatherings
Going out
Talking to strangers
Traveling long distances

questions.prompt: According to the passage, when does the Tortoise's punishment begin?
options: Only during the next banquet
After a full year had passed
From that time forth
Once the Tortoise apologized

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might Jupiter view the Tortoise's absence as a personal insult?
options: The Tortoise was the only animal who chose not to celebrate his marriage
The Tortoise had promised in advance to attend
The Tortoise had insulted Jupiter's wife directly
The Tortoise had convinced other animals to stay home too

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what irony lies in the Tortoise now always carrying his home with him?
options: He no longer has any home to return to
He must now share his home with every other animal
He can no longer enter his home at all
He wanted to stay home, but now he can never truly leave it behind even when he travels

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Tortoise did not "put in an appearance"?
options: He did not speak during the event
He did not show up at the event
He arrived late to the event
He left the event early

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Tortoise is forgiven after explaining why he missed the banquet
A Tortoise is invited to a second banquet as an apology
A Tortoise's preference for staying home earns him a permanent punishment of carrying his house forever
A Tortoise loses his home as punishment for missing the banquet
